The RSI-threshold strategy bought and sold SPY 4 times as its signal changed, while keeping the same $1,000 invested throughout the test. The portfolio grew to $1,086, an 8.6% total return.

The ride was uneven. The portfolio’s worst decline began on December 5, 2025 and lasted until March 30, 2026. From its prior high, it fell 4.8%, or $50. That period matched a broader market correction. The S&P 500 reached a record in late December amid expectations for interest-rate cuts, according to [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/sp-500-hits-intraday-record-high-fueled-by-rate-cut-bets-2025-12-24/). By February, investors were also weighing worries about the cost and disruption of artificial intelligence, renewed tariff uncertainty, and geopolitical tensions, [Reuters reported](https://www.reuters.com/business/us-stock-futures-falter-ai-jitters-nasdaq-braces-steep-monthly-fall-2026-02-27/). In late March, rising oil prices and uncertainty around the Iran conflict added further pressure, with the S&P 500 falling 1.7% on March 26 and reaching a new low for the year on March 30, according to [AP](https://apnews.com/article/wall-street-stocks-dow-nasdaq-9f0c2281f1de0bb4abe66bd568598aa5) and [AP](https://apnews.com/article/wall-street-stocks-dow-nasdaq-800109b3445f87f30865196e08363576).

The recovery was quick after that low. The portfolio reached its highest recorded value on April 14, 2026, when stocks rebounded as oil prices eased and investors returned to technology shares, [Reuters reported](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/global-markets-global-markets-2026-04-14/). Those events provide context for the swings, but the test’s result comes from how the RSI rules moved in and out of SPY during the period.

The meaningful tradeoff was performance. Because the benchmark was SPY itself, the comparison was against simply staying invested in the same asset. The strategy earned 8.6%, while the benchmark earned 16.9%, leaving the strategy behind by 8.3 percentage points. In exchange for its active buying and selling, it experienced a measured 4.8% worst drop, but the test shows that it gave up a substantial amount of the benchmark’s return."}
